chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: The Jade Room opposite Kid Ory
summary: A modern band alternating with Kid Ory's Dixielanders at the Jade Room, owned by 'Mother Goddamn'.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And later on, they booked us into a place farther east on the Boulevard, called The Jade Room. And it wasn't really a Jazz room. They had different kinds of music going on. But when we worked there, we played opposite Kid Ory's band, and a lot of people thought we might have some conflict, you know, with us with this modern-type band and Kid Ory with his Dixieland band. And it worked out beautifully because we all had respect for each other, you know. They had respect for what we were doing, and we had respect for them. We got along beautifully. Like, on the breaks, when we'd pass by, we'd talk with each other, you
know. And it was really, really a nice engagement.
Was that also a restaurant, or was it just a bar?
Because there was a Jade Lounge in (?).
No, this was a big place. It was kind of a big place. Yeah, the Jade Room. In fact, the guy that owned it, he was kind of far out there. He called himself "Mother Goddamn."

Ha-ha! You remember it now, huh, right? Yeah, he was a little bit on the homosexual side. But he loved music, though. He loved the music and treated everybody just beautifully, you know. [LAUGHS] What a name to put on yourself, huh? [LAUGHS]
